data.name: Menahem
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Menahem means 'comforter' or 'consoler'. Derived from the Hebrew words 'men' (consoler) and 'hamech' (God). In the Bible, Menahem was the name of several prophets and kings. He is known for his role in consoling the people of Israel and leading them back to God.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name symbolizes comfort and divine consolation.

in_hebrew.name: מנחם
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מנחם הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'מְנַחֵם', נגזר מהשורש נ-ח-ם שפירושו 'לנחם' או 'לנconsole'. השם מנחם מוזכר בתנ'ך (מלכים ב' טו, טז) כשמו של מלך ישראל. השם מעיד על המשמעות של נחמה, שמחה ועידוד.

in_greek.name: Μενεχμ
in_greek.long_meaning: Μενεχμ είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος מנחם. Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα Μενεχμ συνδέεται με την έννοια της παρηγορήσεως και της χαράς. Στο βιβλικό πλαίσιο, ο Μενεχμ αναφέρεται ως ο βασιλιάς του Ισραήλ (Β΄ Βασιλειών 15:16).

in_latin.name: Menahem
in_latin.long_meaning: Menahem est nomen hebraicum quod in latinum vertitur 'consolator' vel 'gaudens'. Nomen Menahem invenitur in Biblia (2 Regum 15:16) ut nomen regis Israel. Nomen significat consolationem, gaudium et exhortationem.

in_english.name: Menahem
in_english.long_meaning: Menahem is a Hebrew name that means 'comforter' or 'soother'. It is derived from the root 'n-h-m' which means 'to comfort'. In the Bible, Menahem was the name of a king of Israel (2 Kings 15:16). The name has been used in Christian tradition to signify a person who brings comfort, solace, and reassurance. It connotes a sense of peace, tranquility, and joy.

biblical_reference.note: Menahem was a king of Israel who reigned from 748 to 738 BCE.

data.cultural_impact: The name Menahem holds a rich cultural significance in Jewish and Christian traditions. In Jewish history, Menahem is the name of several biblical prophets and kings, including King Menahem of Israel and the prophet Menahem the son of Gad. These leaders were known for their role in providing comfort and guidance to their people during times of uncertainty and hardship. In Christian traditions, the name Menahem is also associated with Menahem the Evangelist, who was said to have preached in Egypt and Ethiopia during the early Christian period.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Menahem carries a deep spiritual significance as it is derived from the Hebrew words meaning 'consoler' or 'comforter'. The name Menahem serves as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there is always hope and comfort to be found in the presence of God. It is a name that inspires compassion, understanding, and a deep sense of empathy for others. It serves as a reminder that as believers, we are called to be a source of comfort and strength to those around us, just as God has been a source of comfort and strength to us. Ultimately, the name Menahem invites us to live out our faith in a tangible and meaningful way, by bringing hope and healing to those who are suffering.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Menahem was a king of Israel in the 16th century BCE. The name Menahem carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Menahem was the son of Gideon and reigned in the northern kingdom of Israel after his father's death. He is known for his military conquests and his alliance with the Assyrians.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Menahem remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Thomas Menahem, a minister in New York, United States, shares that their name Menahem meaning "Comforted by God" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Menahem, meaning "consolation" or "comfort of the earth," embodies the compassionate and nurturing aspect of God in Christian tradition. It serves as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, God's love and grace provide solace and strength.
